name: Tahsan Rahman Khan

global_influences.evidence: Tahsan was formerly the keyboardist and second vocalist of Black, described as a grunge and alternative rock band, giving him a Western rock-idiom foundation prior to his romantic-pop solo career.

local_adaptation_notes: Trained in classical/traditional vocal contexts at Shishu Academy and Chhayanat before joining the alternative rock band Black, Tahsan pivoted to a solo career built on melodic, romantic Bangla pop songwriting (Kothopokothon, 2004) that became broadly popular across generations, later expanding his public profile through television and film acting.
sound_evolution_summary: Formative period (late 1990s–early 2000s): keyboardist and second vocalist for the grunge/alternative rock band Black. Solo breakthrough (2004): debut solo album Kothopokothon launched his career as a romantic pop singer-songwriter. Consolidation period: album Icche and its single 'Alo Alo' became generational anthems; discography expanded to 200+ songs including numerous collaborations, alongside a parallel acting career beginning with the 2004 drama 'Offbeat.'
concert_culture_notes: Prominent presence in Bangladeshi television, telefilm and mainstream media-driven concert/promotional circuits rather than a dedicated touring-band model, reflecting his dual music/acting celebrity status.
listener_community_notes: Represents a key Pop-genre reference artist in the BMEM framework; his romantic, melodic songwriting draws a broad mainstream and youth audience distinct from the harder rock/metal listener communities, with crossover appeal via his acting career.
